Subject: Acme feature parity & proposed next tests

Hi Sara 

Thanks again for the great discussion this morning. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we can move the eval forward: 

- Recap: Acme is focused on three validation areas for parity with your current hyperscaler usage: 1) function/tool calling (reliable structured outputs), 2) streaming latency & partial responses (esp. for long generation/assistant scenarios), and 3) structured output and deterministic parsing for downstream systems.
- What we heard you ask for: a short, reproducible test that compares Redwood against your current API in those areas, and a small Dedicated sandbox for throughput-sensitive streaming tests.

Proposed next steps: 
1) Weve attached a short evaluation plan with suggested tests and acceptance criteria (redwood-acme-eval-plan.pdf).
2) If youre comfortable, well spin up a Dedicated test pool and load the models you commonly use (please confirm model variants).
3) Technical kickoff: Ill loop in Dev (ccd) to own the test harness and results; well share a Drive folder with scripts & test data.

Differentiators to call out for Acme: automatic KV/prefix caching (reduces token cost for chat-like flows), streaming function-call support (partial function args while streaming), and explicit tooling for quantization/throughput tradeoffs so you can tune price vs latency. Well include a short feature matrix in the Drive link.

Can you confirm: 1) Which model variants you want us to mirror, and 2) a preferred date/time for a 3045m technical kickoff next week?

Thanks  looking forward to moving fast.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference

Attachments: redwood-acme-eval-plan.pdf

Hi Marissa 

Thanks for the clear recap and the plan (I opened the PDF and it looks good at a glance). A few clarifications from our side before we lock in the kickoff: 

1) Model variants: We primarily use acme-llm-large (baseline), and weve been testing a trimmed 7B quantized variant for cost-sensitive endpoints. If you can mirror acme-llm-large and a 7B-q equivalent that would be ideal.
2) Streaming SLA: For our use case, end-to-end median partial-response latency must be <= 200ms for short messages (under 1k tokens) and p95 under 400ms. Well include a small workload file.
3) Function/tool calling: We need deterministic structured JSON outputs for invoicing and attribution flows. Examples are in the Drive doc Ill upload after this message.

Also looping in John from procurement (cc) for any SOW/PO questions  he may ask for a short SOW and a DocuSign to sign the test sandbox agreement.

Were available for a technical kickoff on Wed Jul 1 or Thu Jul 2 between 101312 PT.

Sara

Marissa / Camila 

I reviewed the Drive eval plan and attached a short feature matrix (acme-feature-matrix.csv). Notes: 
- For streaming p95 targets (<= 400ms), H100 nodes with our continuous batching disabled for that pool will be the safest to hit p95. We can also tune tile-size and use lower-precision kernels.
- For function calling: Redwood supports streaming function args (we can emit partial JSON chunks as streaming updates and then finalize). We should include a test that streams a function call with incremental JSON patches and validate partial-parse behavior.
- For structured output determinism: add a seeded-regeneration test and a simple schema-validation harness; Ill add scripts into the Drive folder.

Ask: please authorize a Dedicated sandbox for 48 hours with 2 H100 nodes; Ill need access to the model artifacts you want mirrored and a contact at Acme for network allowlist.

Attaching: acme-feature-matrix.csv

Dev
